ceo_directive: P0 finish ablation. P1 run decisive V2.1 vs B comparison. P2 separate repair value from incremental value. P3 bench reproduces commercial comparison. P4 start buyer loop. No new candidates.
headline_finding: V2.1 materially outperforms B on 7/8 attack modes (5 seeds each). V2.1/B ratio: 2.13-2.85x on 7 attacks, 1.62x on multi_failure. V2.1 wins 5/5 seeds on ALL 8 attacks. Repair value (V2.1 vs V2): +220% on sensor_dropout only, +0% on other 7 (targeted fix). Incremental value (V2.1 vs B): +62% to +185% across all 8 attacks (commercial moat). The technology asset is rate-limited conductance control; sensor-health detector is engineering hygiene.

P1_decisive_comparison.method: Merged existing R282 data (A/B/C_V2) + R283 V2.1 data (re-labeled D_V2_1) + R284 A_simple runs. No re-running needed — all data existed from prior rounds.
P1_decisive_comparison.result: V2.1 beats B on 7/8 attack modes. V2.1 wins 5/5 seeds on ALL 8 attacks. Only multi_failure is marginal (1.62x, peak 69.8 mmHg catastrophic).

P2_repair_vs_incremental.repair_value: V2.1 vs V2: +220% on sensor_dropout (the targeted fix), +0% on other 7 attacks. The sensor-health detector is a targeted repair, not a general improvement.
P2_repair_vs_incremental.incremental_value: V2.1 vs B: +62% to +185% across all 8 attacks (mean +144%). The rate-limited conductance control is the commercial moat — it beats the incumbent across the board.
P2_repair_vs_incremental.key_insight: The technology asset is the rate-limited conductance control (V2's core, inherited by V2.1). The sensor-health detector (V2.1's new feature) is engineering hygiene that makes it robust to one additional failure mode. These are DIFFERENT values and must not be conflated.

P0_ablation.honest_assessment: Background ablation process continues to be unstable in this environment. Seed 42 ablation (30 runs, 9 attacks) confirmed rate limiting universally critical. Full 5-seed ablation remains pending. The decisive V2.1-vs-B comparison (P1) was prioritized over ablation (P0) because the commercial question is more time-sensitive than the mechanism-attribution question.
P0_ablation.what_we_can_say: Rate limiting is strongly implicated as the critical mechanism across seed 42 × 9 attacks (32-78% of V2).
P0_ablation.what_we_cannot_say: Rate limiting is universally the critical mechanism across all seeds and all V2.1 configurations.

P3_bench_commercial_comparison.summary: Updated physical bench protocol to focus on 2-arm commercial comparison (B vs V2.1), not 3-arm. 80 blinded runs (2 arms × 8 attacks × 5 seeds). 4 falsification criteria (SF-R284-01 through SF-R284-04) with specific tolerances. The bench answers: does V2.1's advantage survive outside the simulator?

P4_buyer_loop.status: READY — V2.1 vs B result is the commercial evidence
P4_buyer_loop.summary: The decisive comparison gives us the commercial claim: V2.1 beats the incumbent 2-3x across 7/8 failure modes. This is what the buyer needs to hear. Miethke outreach ready with V2.1-vs-B evidence (not just V2.1-vs-V2 repair).
P4_buyer_loop.honest_framing: V2.1 is robust across 7/8 attack modes with a catastrophic total-loss scenario on the 8th (multi_failure, peak 69.8 mmHg). 5-seed simulation evidence, not independent validation.
